issue.body:
# Sorry. The website is infected by AdShield, Inc.

Unfortunately, It is complicated to resolve with a regular adblock rule because the website is being protected by service of Ad-Shield that is an anti-adblock company.

## Userscript Installation
Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On likebus.ua the site pins two fixed app-promotion bars over the mobile page (an install bar at the top, which the reporter boxed, and an app-download bar at the bottom covering results); the rule likebus.ua#⁠#⁠#⁠likebus-app-banner, #⁠appStickyBottom hides both and was verified in the filtered browser with the page left intact. I placed it in the Mobile App Banners filter, which is where this repository keeps app-install banner rules. ## Rule `likebus.ua###likebus-app-banner, #appStickyBottom` ## Policy rationale Not the site's own paid advertising or a paywall:⁠ the target is the site's app-install/app-download promotion, which the AdGuard Mobile App Banners annoyance filter exists to remove and which the reporter filed as an Annoyance. Not an anti-adblock wall, scam or phishing page:⁠ the page loads normally with its content, and no detector script or gate is involved. The two fixed bars consume \~140px of an 812px mobile viewport and cover the site header and the first result cards, so the policy exception for unobtrusive non-animated header banners does not apply. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f2c955ffc54a331e71160a8315d6715c533b6419/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The events page at restaurantcounter.co.uk shows a self-hosted CookieConsent ("We use cookies!") card fixed over the page plus its floating cookie-settings button. The verified rule restaurantcounter.co.uk#⁠#⁠#⁠cc--main, #⁠cookie-settings hides both, leaves the page intact, and belongs with the existing cookie-notice rules in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt. ## Rule `restaurantcounter.co.uk###cc--main, #cookie-settings` ## Policy rationale The report is a first-party cookie-consent notice overlapping page content; none of the run instruction's closing rules apply (not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, not a scam/phishing page). It is not an anti-adblock wall at all, so no detector-script gate applies. Element hiding is the least invasive fix and matches the maintainer guidance to hide the notice when that is enough; it is also a basic CSS-selector rule, so it works in the reporter's Safari content-blocker model as well as the browser extension and desktop apps. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f2c955ffc54a331e71160a8315d6715c533b6419/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41766717517 Automated analysis against filters at `f2c955f`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — bus.tickets.ua shows a full-width app-install promo bar ("Travel easier with our app" + "Use app" Play Store button + close X) at the very top of every page, directly above the site header; the reporter circled exactly that bar. Hiding it with bus.tickets.ua#⁠#⁠.app-top-banner was verified in the AdGuard CLI baseline (bar visible, then hidden with no leftover gap, page intact) and is filed in the Mobile App Banners filter. ## Rule `bus.tickets.ua##.app-top-banner` ## Policy rationale The report is a mobile-app-install banner annoyance, the category the AdGuard Mobile App Banners filter is defined to block; none of the run instruction's close rules (site's own third-party advertising, paywalls, German anti-adblock wall, anti-adblock without a captured detector script, scam/phishing page) applies. The Mobile App Banners policy limitation on non-animated header/menu banners was weighed:⁠ the element is a full-width standalone promo strip with its own CTA and close control placed above, not inside, the site's header element, so it is treated as blockable; the judgment is recorded for the reviewing maintainer. No existing filter expression covers the element (no rule for .app-top-banner or #⁠app-top-banner; the shared #⁠#⁠.app-banner family uses a different class), so a new cosmetic rule is required rather than an extension. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f2c955ffc54a331e71160a8315d6715c533b6419/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On tokubai.co.jp a full-screen first-party campaign/app-download popup (div.popup_banner_image) covers the leaflet page while a web2app cover clips the leaflet gallery and locks body scroll. A domain-scoped trusted-click-element scriptlet that dismisses the popup and the 'このままウェブで見る' app-gate was verified in the CLI proxy:⁠ popup gone, leaflet fully rendered and scroll restored, page integrity intact. ## Rule `tokubai.co.jp#%#//scriptlet('trusted-click-element', '.popup_banner_image .close_button.close_popup, .cover_web2app__read_more_on_web', '', '1000')` ## Policy rationale The reported overlay is the site's own campaign/app-download promo gated over the leaflet content, handled under the annoyance filters' stated purposes (Popups:⁠ popups that introduce the site's features; Mobile App Banners:⁠ banners that promote the site's mobile app), not first-party ad inventory, so the 'first-party advertising' carve-out does not close it. Element hiding was tried first (tokubai.co.jp#⁠#⁠.popup_banner_image) and was not enough because the app-install cover and the clipped leaflet survived; a scriptlet that dismisses the gate is the justified next step under the maintainer rule 'hide the popup when that is enough'. No policy rule blocks rule generation for this annoyance report, and the rule is domain-scoped to tokubai.co.jp. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/95db9bb4cd80f84d92692158b30448ff9cf9707b/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41770217989 Automated analysis against filters at `95db9bb`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://chat.mozilla.org/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchat.mozilla.org%2F) ### Comment > The AdGuard CookieNotices filterlist contains a cosmetic filter that interferes with the Element Web client for Matrix. I an demosnstrating this on the web client hosted at chat.mozilla.org, but likely other instances of this popular web client are also affected. > > When you log in to your Matrix account from a new device, you are strongly advised to verify the new login from another device where you were already logged in. This verification is requried for encrypted messages to become readable, among other purposes. > The interfering filtering rule (`.mx_ToastContainer`) ends up hiding the popup where the user is supposed to accept or decline the verification request. The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Not reproduced — The reported Bing search ad cannot be reproduced:⁠ the unfiltered control and the reporter's own filter configuration both load the reported query with only organic results (no ad container, no ad label, no ad request in the HAR), and complete full-page vision of the current extension session reports the symptom absent. Recommending closure as not reproduced; the reporter's unverified "Silver Fox trojan" claim about the linked domain, which now ranks organically, is left for a maintainer.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

No rule of the run instruction's filter policy closes this report:⁠ the reported problem is not a paywall, not a German or other anti-adblock wall, and not a first-party ad of a content site (the only candidate location, the advertiser's own destination, is a third-party site), so rule generation was allowed for this run. The reported defect could not be produced:⁠ no ad instance, ad label or ad placeholder appears on the loaded reported page in either environment, so there is no rule to write for it.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"5f76589bc6d86a35b1c1f0eb4095d6eb98b287dd569013649364f72fb7ef542f"} -->
The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — In two live sessions of onlineradiobox.com (desktop en-US and mobile ja-JP, complete full-page vision) through the AdGuard CLI baseline the reported anti-adblock modal never appears:⁠ the page loads fully, no such dialog exists in the DOM or the page text, and no Ad-Shield/html-load detector request is made, while AdGuard Base already injects the Ad-Shield countermeasure scriptlets for this domain. The report could not be reproduced and no new rule has evidence behind it, so it is recommended for closing.

## Policy rationale

The run instruction's closing rules do not apply to this report:⁠ it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and the wall in the reporter's screenshot is a Japanese-language anti-adblock modal on a US-domain site, so the 'German anti-adblock wall' close rule does not cover it. Because no repository rule closes this report, the run recorded allow_rule_generation; rule generation was open, but no rule could be derived or validated because the reported defect was absent in every environment this run could execute. The instruction's anti-adblock gate ('write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer') was also unmet:⁠ the captured request inventory of both loaded sessions contains no html-load.com / Ad-Shield detector request at all, so no new anti-adblock rule has evidence behind it.

## Missing information

- No way to load the reporter's settings import in the adguard_cli route: Issue #⁠246218 carries a reporter settings import URL (AdGuard for Android profile with Fanboy's Annoyances and two custom subscriptions). The locked adguard_cli environment declares those third-party sources as skippedSources, and `launch_browser` refuses `settings` for an `extension:"none"` session ("A control session (extension \⁠"none\⁠") runs no blocker and takes no \⁠"settings\⁠""), offering only an `extension:"prepared"` blocker instead. The run instruction gives no way to form a `reported_on_current` reporter-parity session in the CLI route, so the reporter's exact configuration cannot be compared with the CLI baseline and the controlled reporter-vs-defaults comparison the instruction asks for cannot be run.

## Artifacts

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter-circled defect on nwknews.jp is a sponsored Amazon "Fire TV Stick 4K Select" product card (rel="nofollow sponsored" Amazon links, product image from m.media-amazon.com) injected inside the article body; no baseline rule hides it. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule was verified in the AdGuard CLI proxy:⁠ the card was visible before and gone after, with no remaining instances, no page damage and no ad-layout residue. ## Rule `nwknews.jp##div[class^="article-body"] table[style*="border:1px solid #ddd"]` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's closing rules cover first-party self-promotion, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls and anti-adblock walls without a captured detector script; this report is none of those. The reported element is a sponsored affiliate product card (rel="nofollow sponsored", Amazon Associates tag omosironetton-22) inserted into the article body, not the site's editorial content or its own products, and the Japanese filter already blocks the same class of Amazon affiliate unit on nwknews.jp. The symptom is reproduced on the filtered baseline and the candidate rule was verified by the environment experiment with an intact page. ## Place in the list [JapaneseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/2ce65f5aeeb216e53e01efdea5828ffdfd535789/JapaneseFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 846](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/2ce65f5aeeb216e53e01efdea5828ffdfd535789/JapaneseFilter/sections/specific.txt#L846). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported Netflix watch page is unreachable in this run:⁠ /watch/81011359 302-redirects to the non-member title page for 뤼팽 both in the reporter-settings proxy session and in an extension-less CLI-route session, and no Netflix session is available, so the circled playback area was never observable (full-page vision confirms the marketing/title page, not the watch page). The only rule decisions on that page were tracker blocks (||netflix.com/log/, ||netflix.com/api/ftl/probe?monotonic=, ||onetrust.com^$third-party), and since the report names no broken element, no evidence-backed rule can be proposed or validated.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's annotated region on fonbet.by/sports is the full-width cookie-consent bar fixed at the bottom of the page, and the baseline filters leave it visible; the rule `fonbet.by##div[class^="cookie-alert"]` hides it (merging into the repository's existing shared selector) with no layout damage. Verified in the A/B/C experiment:⁠ selector visible on the baseline page, hidden with the candidate, page integrity intact. ## Rule `fonbet.by##div[class^="cookie-alert"]` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's filter policy closes only first-party advertising, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls, and anti-adblock reports without a captured detector script; the reporter-defined target here is a cookie-consent notice, not any of those, and no anti-adblock wall, paywall or third-party ad appears on the page. The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to block cookie notices and CMP requests, and the maintainer rules allow a cosmetic hide when the page then works — the verified after-state shows the page fully functional with the bar removed. The repository already carries the identical selector for gameplay.pl, so the fix belongs to that shared rule family and the host merges the fonbet.by-scoped candidate into it. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/9203aed27915efeb09b00a9c6c447dc0f2da9de5/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reported annoyance on www⁠.bursasaati.com.tr is the site's fixed bottom cookie-consent bar (div.js-cookie-consent.cookie-consent) that the reporter's screenshot arrow points at. Plain element hiding cannot hide it because the widget carries inline "display:⁠ block !important", so the verified fix is the domain-scoped extended-CSS rule "bursasaati.com.tr#⁠?#⁠.js-cookie-consent", which the host merges into the existing shared #⁠?#⁠.js-cookie-consent family in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt. ## Rule `bursasaati.com.tr#?#.js-cookie-consent` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent notice annoyance, which the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter covers; it is not first-party site advertising, not a paywall and not a German anti-adblock wall. No anti-adblock, paywall or product-bug rule of the run instruction applies; the reporter's enabled filter set includes AdGuard Cookie Notices (filter 18), which the executable baseline provides. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/9203aed27915efeb09b00a9c6c447dc0f2da9de5/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 1149](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/9203aed27915efeb09b00a9c6c447dc0f2da9de5/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L1149). ## Screenshots

issue.title: French filter: remove affiliate.json exception fixed upstream
issue.body:
Liste FR has narrowed the source rule in easylist/listefr@0ceb87826a (easylist/listefr#309):

```diff
-/affiliate.js$domain=~mercari.com
+/affiliate.js|$domain=~mercari.com
```

The rule now only matches URLs ending in `affiliate.js`, so it no longer blocks `affiliate.json` localization files. The site-specific exception added for #246033 is therefore no longer needed, and this PR removes it.

comment.body: @Alex-302 Could you please take a look when you have a moment? Liste FR has fixed the rule upstream, so this PR now just removes the exception added for #246033. Thanks!

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The cookie notice fixed at the bottom-left of info.2gis.ru/download (the banner the reporter arrowed) is still shown with the reporter's filter set, and it is served with the page's own HTML/JS. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule matched only that banner and the verified experiment hid it with the page left intact. ## Rule `info.2gis.ru##div:has(> button[aria-label*="cookie"])` ## Policy rationale The report is an ordinary cookie consent notice (issue comment 'cookie', screenshot showing the cookie banner), not the site's own advertising, not a paywall and not a German anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's closing rules applies. The filter policy states the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter is designed to block cookie notices, so a rule belongs in this repository. Maintainer rule satisfied:⁠ hiding the popup is enough — the page content stays fully usable and no scroll lock remains (html/body overflow visible, document height 1456px before and after). ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/cfbb2bbcd8e3716c329fb090610401ee452d395d/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41799769155 Automated analysis against filters at `cfbb2bb`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reported annoyance on www⁠.novostroy.su is a first-party fixed cookie-consent bar whose CSS-module class no longer matches the existing novostroy.*#⁠#⁠div[⁠class^="Cookie_wrapper"]⁠ rule. Adding novostroy.su#⁠#⁠div[⁠class^="Cookie-module-scss-module__"]⁠ to the Cookie Notices filter was verified:⁠ the bar is visible on the baseline and gone after the rule, with page integrity intact. ## Rule `novostroy.su##div[class^="Cookie-module-scss-module__"]` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's closure list (the site's own advertising, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls) does not cover this report:⁠ it is an ordinary cookie-consent notice, not an ad, paywall or anti-adblock wall, and the page shows no anti-adblock detection. The filter policy's AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists precisely to block cookie notices on web pages, so rule generation is open. No rule in the repository matches the site's current cookie-banner class family, so a new site-scoped cosmetic rule is required rather than an extension of a shared rule. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/b78ab920a9111e81cbcfe0feb784d84a2faea797/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"4017b4a51f13832b970fca2a2c419b899a49b52519b92e66bce437ee5bc60313"} -->
The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported CHECK24 cookie-consent modal does not appear on https:⁠//www⁠.check24.de/ in the reporter-list baseline:⁠ the repository's existing Cookie Notices scriptlet `check24.*#%#//scriptlet('trusted-set-cookie-reload', 'c24consent', 'f')` is applied, the `c24consent` cookie is set, and full-page vision plus DOM probes find no consent element, so no new rule is needed and the report can be closed.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction filter policy:⁠ none of its close rules applies here. The report is not first-party advertising, not a paywall, and the page shows no ad-blocker detection wall — it is a cookie-consent notice, so the German anti-adblock carve-out (a German site's wall or popup that detects the ad blocker) is not triggered, and the instruction's 'otherwise hand to a maintainer' branch for anti-adblock walls does not apply because no detector was reported or found. AdGuard Cookie Notices filter policy (filter-policy.md):⁠ the filter is designed to block cookie notices and CMP requests, so a cookie notice on www⁠.check24.de is in scope for rule generation. Rule generation is permitted; the close is recommended on reproduction grounds, not on a policy gate:⁠ the reported notice is absent on the successfully loaded reported page under the current lists.

## Artifacts

## Reproduced symptom

The banner never rendered in this runner's sessions (UHF host empty, mscc hasConsent()=true, full-page vision:⁠ symptom absent), so the rule could not be validated and is carried for human review.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On qiita.com's Advent Calendar page the Social Media filter already hides the Facebook and Hatena share buttons but the X (Twitter) share button stays visible, matching the reporter's screenshot. The candidate rule qiita.com#⁠#⁠button[⁠aria-label="ポスト"]⁠ was verified in the extension experiment:⁠ the X share icon disappears while the page stays intact. ## Rule `qiita.com##button[aria-label="ポスト"]` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The reported element is an X/Twitter share button in a share row — a social Share widget covered by the stated purpose of the AdGuard Social Media filter. Not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's closing rules applies. The repository already hides the two sibling share buttons of the same row on qiita.com, so blocking the remaining one is consistent with existing practice. ## Place in the list [SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/6cf9e3e2dffd83a7e1f92cbea72c4fbea5060c85/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 13](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/6cf9e3e2dffd83a7e1f92cbea72c4fbea5060c85/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt#L13). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reported annoyance is the site's own cookie-consent card together with a full-page dark backdrop that dims and blocks the hotel room-availability page; both are first-party markup with no third-party CMP request behind them. One extended-CSS element-hiding rule anchored on the component's data-testid/data-slot attributes hid both with page integrity intact and was verified against the live page, so it belongs in the Cookie Notices filter. ## Rule `evo-ibe.uk.hos.accessacloud.com#?#div:has(> div[data-slot="card"] [data-testid="accept-all-button"]), div.fixed.inset-0:has(+ div [data-testid="accept-all-button"])` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie notice (AdGuard Cookie Notices filter purpose), not first-party advertising, a paywall or an anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's close rules applies. The symptom is baked into first-party markup with no distinct vendor request, so an element-hiding rule in the Cookie Notices filter is the repository's own fix family; no maintainer-ruled close rule applies. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/977504747692887414af62c53dcafc1f06d57637/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41818553633 Automated analysis against filters at `9775047`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On jp.ign.com the article page still shows its social share widget row (the bar with the rounded シェア share button) between the article body and the "Related" section, and no enabled list hides it. The reported element is a social share widget, which is the stated purpose of the AdGuard Social Media filter (third-party Like/Share widgets), and maintainers already hide the same IGN share control (hide-in-shadow-dom button[⁠data-testid="ShareBtn"]⁠ for ign.com) and the identical .video-actions container for javgiga.com. Fixed upstream, pending the extension release

## Reproduced symptom

Reproduced — The reporter's arrowed element is eiga.com's first-party app-install banner (div.promo-banner ⁠> a.web_to_app_open_btn, media.eiga.com/.../webToAppTheater.jpg) directly below the region accordion, and the repository already carries the exact rule eiga.com#⁠#⁠.promo-banner in AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt. The pinned extension's released lists still show that banner, while the identical rule verified in the browser experiment removes it with page integrity intact, so no new rule is needed - only the released filter build catching up.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Missing information

- No way to read list-file section headers or build inclusion of a repository section: The run's tools expose the repository only through search_rules (rule text + file path + section name). No tool returns a list file's section headers, its `!#if`/build gating, or which sections ship in the published filter build. That matters here:⁠ the repository contains `eiga.com##.promo-banner` (AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt, line 4812, section "Mobile apps - Mobile sites only"), yet the run's pinned AdGuard Browser Extension 5.5.2.3 with the reporter's enabled lists (AdGuard Mobile App Banners = 4415 released lines) does not apply it and the banner stays visible. I therefore cannot tell whether the released build simply predates the rule or whether that section is excluded from the build, which decides between "fixed upstream, pending release" and "maintainer must move the rule".

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — www⁠.kacakspor5.com pushes the HADIBET betting brand:⁠ the header logo and "Canlı Bahis Yap" link open the betting site hadi.life in a new tab and a HADIBET bet promo is painted as the stream player's background, while the Turkish filter already blocks the site's ad API and hides the pageskin, player logo and splash banner. No candidate could be verified — hiding the ad links left the video ad (or removed the header logo the review counts as damage), and the repository's own `.player-poster` background-removal fix targets an element inside the player iframe, which the probe cannot measure.

## Candidate for review

`www.kacakspor5.com#$#.player-poster { background-image: none !important; }`

TurkishFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule never judged this candidate:⁠ the probe reads the top document only and `.player-poster` is rendered inside the same-domain `/izle` player iframe, so the experiment ended with `baseline_symptom_absent` (unmatchedBaselineSelector `.player-poster`) and exhausted the run's candidate attempts. The selector is the repository's own established fix for this player template (TurkishFilter/sections/specific.txt lines 6072 and 6447, `#$#.player-poster { background-image: none [!important] }`, and the trgoals list at 6464), and the CSS-injection gate was met by the previous experiment, whose bound review reported a page-integrity regression when `.player-poster` itself was hidden (empty black player panel).

## Missing information

- No instruction on verifying cosmetic rules whose target lives in a same-domain iframe: The reported "video background ad" on www⁠.kacakspor5.com is the CSS background of `.player-poster` inside the same-domain player iframe (`/izle?id=…`). The repository's own fix family for that element (TurkishFilter/sections/specific.txt, e.g. `[$domain=/trgoals\d+\.xyz$/]#$#.player-poster { background-image: none !important; }` and the trgoals list at line 6464) is therefore the natural rule to add the reported domain to, but apply_rule's probe reads the top document only and ended the experiment with `baseline_symptom_absent` for the selector `.player-poster`, spending the last candidate attempt. The run instruction gives no way to scope or verify a cosmetic candidate whose element is rendered inside an iframe (no revealSteps that would help, since the frame loads with the page), so the only maintainer-backed fix could not be validated.

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Issue #⁠246259 reports an in-app ad banner ('CONFERENCE LEAGUE FANTASY', small 'Ad' label) inside the native Sofascore Android app, but the run's only URL is the Google Play listing:⁠ that page loads cleanly with no ad slots, its HAR has no Sofascore ad request, and navigation to sofascore.com is refused. The request behind the in-app banner could not be observed, so no evidence-backed rule is possible and this stays analysis-only.

## Missing information

- No capability to capture in-app (native Android app) ad traffic for issue #⁠246259: Issue #⁠246259 reports an ad banner inside the native Android app com.sofascore.results (AdGuard for Android, VPN mode); its only "Issue URL" is the Google Play listing. In the locked adguard_cli environment the session may navigate only to the issue origin (play.google.com):⁠ open_page to sofascore.com was refused with 'URL must remain on configured issue origin', and the proxy HAR of the Play Store page contains no Sofascore or ad-network request (only play.google.com, gstatic, play-lh, googletagmanager/google-analytics blocked by Tracking Protection). No browser or CLI surface in this run can run the Android app or its ad SDK, so the request that renders the reported banner cannot be observed, and no evidence-backed network rule (for example a $app=com.sofascore.results rule) can be derived. It's being hidden or removed by a rule in the AdGuard Popups filter list, and I believe that's wrong, because that list is meant to target pop-ups, and this element isn't one. comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — madridinforma.es keeps three empty pale-gray AdSense slots (250 px main column, 300 px sidebar, 200 px below the article photo) because the site's own CSS reserves the space while the third-party ad unit is blocked. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule on the containers that hold those ad wrappers removes all three in the verified A/B/C experiment with page integrity intact. ## Rule `madridinforma.es##div:has(> .mi-ad-header), div:has(> .mi-ad-sidebar), div:has(> #mi-ad-post)` ## Policy rationale Reported symptom is leftover empty third-party AdSense ad placeholders (ca-pub-7503386554994687), not the site's own first-party advertising, so the 'no rule for first-party ads' policy does not apply. Not a paywall and not an anti-adblock wall:⁠ the page shows no detection message, popup or content gate, and the reporter's screenshot and the live page show no such element. Rule is a domain-scoped element-hiding rule on empty ad containers, i.e. removal of ad leftovers, which the policy's ad-blocking criteria allow; no JavaScript rule is involved. ## Place in the list [SpanishFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/511b7fa1a042a5b51a19900bb40461a5ebf205ae/SpanishFilter/sections/specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41831350921 Automated analysis against filters at `511b7fa`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — tour.ne.jp/j_air/ serves two site-owned app-install promos — the pinned top banner the reporter arrowed and a full-screen app-promotion sheet over the booking form — with no third-party loader behind them. One cosmetic rule, tour.ne.jp#⁠#⁠.cmn-app-bnr-header, .cmn-modal-app, was verified hiding both with the page intact. ## Rule `tour.ne.jp##.cmn-app-bnr-header, .cmn-modal-app` ## Policy rationale The reported defect is a site-owned mobile-app promotion (banner + full-screen app-install sheet), not first-party advertising, so the 'site's own advertising:⁠ no rule' policy does not apply and AdGuard Mobile App Banners exists to block exactly these. Not a paywall and not a German anti-adblock wall; no anti-adblock wall is present (apply_rule reported antiAdblockDetected false and the page shows no detector notice). The symptom is baked into the first-party HTML with no distinct request behind it, so no anti-adblock gate and no dangerous-page handling applies; a cosmetic rule is the permitted fix. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/511b7fa1a042a5b51a19900bb40461a5ebf205ae/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41829765814 Automated analysis against filters at `511b7fa`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body: That's pretty odd. According to AdGuard's descriptions of its Annoyances filter categories, the AdGuard Popups filter list is not supposed to block such elements, and its name alone suggests it only targets pop-ups. If anything, the AdGuard Other Annoyances filter list should be the one blocking them instead. This element isn't a pop-up. It's an inline newsletter signup form that just stays in place in the footer, so it doesn't fit the Popups category at all. Is blocking this really what the Popups filter list is intended for? If so, it's blocking things beyond its own description, and that should be corrected. Would you please consider this? Thanks.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Two server-rendered KCRA 3 app-download promotions (the "Take our news with you / Download the KCRA 3 app for iOS or Android" card and the weather-map "Download our app for nearby event alerts!" badge strip) are real annoyances that no enabled list hides, but every `##` candidate I validated left the section's own 378x417px grid track empty, which the vision review refused as ad-layout residue, so no rule could be verified.

## Candidate for review

`kcra.com##div[aria-label*="App Promo"], div:has(> div > a > img[alt*="app download"])`

AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule in the reporter settings profile measured the candidate hiding both in-page app-download promotions (status visible-⁠>hidden), pageIntegrity intact and observedDamage empty, but the dedicated visual review returned verdict 'rejected' with adLayoutResidue present and symptom 'not_resolved':⁠ after removal the section keeps its own empty 378x417px first grid track. A rerun with four domChecks confirmed the leftover is the page's own CSS - the promo article is transparent with min-height:⁠410px inside a fixed 3-column grid whose 768px weather-map item and 1158px next item cannot reflow into the emptied cell - and the review still refused, so no candidate could be verified.

## Still visible after the rule

- HAPPENING NEAR YOU section, left column beside the map — Large empty left-column reserved area where the app-download promotion card belongs; no dark card, poster, heading, or blue DOWNLOAD button is visible, leaving a blank app-promo footprint beside the map.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — kcci.com serves a self-promo app-download card in its homepage news grid ("Take our news with you" / "Download the KCCI 8 News app for iOS or Android" / DOWNLOAD → /apps), matching the reporter's "App download" screenshot. Hiding the card's grid item with kcci.com#⁠#⁠article:⁠has(⁠> div[⁠data-button="/apps"]⁠) was verified in the AdGuard browser extension:⁠ the card is gone, the page's grid reflows with no residue and page integrity stays intact. ## Rule `kcci.com##article:has(> div[data-button="/apps"])` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a site app-install banner, the category the filter policy assigns to the AdGuard Mobile App Banners filter ('blocks banners and popups that encourage visitors to install mobile apps'); it is not the site's own third-party advertising, not a paywall and not an anti-adblock wall, so none of the close-without-a-rule cases applies. The banner sits inline in the homepage content grid, not in a header or menu strip, so the Mobile App Banners limitation for non-animated header/menu banners does not exempt it. kcci.com clears the traffic criterion (major Hearst/CBS-affiliated Des Moines news station). ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/6d3bfc900e3a70bac964e1a5710c3270e7f9268b/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's screenshot shows PYMNTS' in-article self-promotion card ("Get more PYMNTS in your Google feed" with Follow PYMNTS / Add as preferred source links) repeating mid-article on www⁠.pymnts.com. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule for the card's container was verified live:⁠ four instances removed, no leftover gap, page integrity intact. ## Rule `pymnts.com##.mid-content-graphic:has(> aside.ps-preferred-source)` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The run instruction's closing rules (first-party ads, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls) do not apply to the reported element:⁠ it is a site self-promotion card, not an ad sold by the site, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall (the page shows no detector overlay or blocker message; antiAdblockDetected=false in both experiment phases). Filter policy for the AdGuard Other Annoyances filter explicitly allows 'Block self-promotion of websites ... if it is considered an annoying element', and the repository itself files PYMNTS' own subscribe promos plus the shared Google-News follow rule '#⁠#⁠.google-news' (subscriptions_specific.txt, line 32) under AnnoyancesFilter subscriptions, so this kind of rule is accepted here. The AdGuard Widgets filter explicitly does not block 'Widgets for self-promotion and site-specific promotional activities', so the rule is deliberately not placed there; the Social Media filter's 'links to the website's social media pages are not blocked' limitation describes that filter's scope only, and no site-wide social links are touched by this wrapper-scoped rule. The candidate was verified live against the reporter's baseline settings:⁠ environmentExperiment=verified with symptom resolved, no remaining instances, page integrity intact and no observed damage. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/3247e80f90f53f26942930bd0e329cb00d49dbbc/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — solidbackup.net shows its own fixed cookie-consent bar ("COOKIES &⁠ PRIVACY" with DECLINE/ACCEPT) pinned over the bottom of every page, which is the annoyance the reporter's screenshot shows. The domain-scoped element-hiding rule solidbackup.net#⁠#⁠div#⁠sb-cookie-banner removed it in the browser experiment (symptom resolved, page integrity intact), so it belongs in the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter's site-specific section. ## Rule `solidbackup.net##div#sb-cookie-banner` ## Policy rationale The fix is a cookie notice, which is exactly what the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to block (filter-policy 'Annoyance filters' section); no exclusion in the policy applies — the site's own advertising, paywalls and anti-adblock walls are not involved. Quality requirements are met:⁠ a static cosmetic rule, no performance impact, no unblocking, no JavaScript rule. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/3247e80f90f53f26942930bd0e329cb00d49dbbc/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The annotated annoyance on www⁠.tiguanforum.de is WoltLab's cookie-notice bar (div.userNotice ⁠> p.info), so I propose the domain-scoped cosmetic rule tiguanforum.de#⁠#⁠.userNotice ⁠> p.info in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt, verified in the reporter-settings session with the bar hidden, no remaining instances and page integrity intact. The existing shared #⁠#⁠.userNotice rule was deliberately not extended to this domain because the site's unclosed userNotice wrapper contains the entire forum content. ## Rule `tiguanforum.de##.userNotice > p.info` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie notice ('Cookie', T:⁠ Annoyance), which the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to hide; no policy exclusion in the run instruction applies. It is not a German anti-adblock wall:⁠ the page shows no ad-blocker detection, wall or popup asking the user to disable the blocker - the annotated element is a plain first-party WoltLab consent bar baked into the served HTML. Not a paywall, not first-party advertising, no scam/phishing content. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/3247e80f90f53f26942930bd0e329cb00d49dbbc/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — duck.ai shows a floating "Help Us Improve / Take Survey" survey card linking out to a third-party survey host and overlapping the chat landing page; baseline lists already carry five duck.ai rules but none covers it. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule anchored on the survey link verified clean in the before/after experiment (symptom resolved, no remaining instances, page integrity intact). ## Rule `duck.ai##div:has(> a[href^="https://selfserve.decipherinc.com/survey/"])` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's policy closes first-party ads, paywalls and German anti-adblock walls, and gates other anti-adblock walls on a captured detector script; none applies here — the reported defect is an unsolicited third-party survey prompt popup, which the AdGuard Popups filter policy explicitly covers ('popups and forms for subscribing to news, promotions, and various events, including third-party channels' and 'other types of popups that may annoy users'). duck.ai is a high-traffic site and the survey card links to an external survey vendor, so the common-criteria traffic and quality requirements are met; the rule is a single cosmetic element-hiding rule with no JavaScript. The symptom is not a content gate:⁠ the page's content and input box stay usable before and after, so neither the consent-gate nor the anti-adblock policy applies. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/3247e80f90f53f26942930bd0e329cb00d49dbbc/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41877848863 Automated analysis against filters at `3247e80`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"25e8ec38d118c48430aeeaeaf4b60304f4195a326511b12d4f676684759d36dd"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — On kitco.com the reporter's blank bands are the page's two reserved in-article ad slots (div#⁠in-content-1, div#⁠in-content-2, 280px each, shown below the 1024px breakpoint) plus the site's own empty comments placeholder. A domain-scoped hide of the empty ad slots removed the reported in-body bands with no remaining instances, but the bound vision review rejected the candidate for page damage that the selector provably cannot cause, so the rule goes to a human unverified.

## Candidate for review

`kitco.com##div[id^="in-content-"]:empty`

BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule never rejected this rule:⁠ environmentExperiment was inconclusive with failedCandidateChecks empty, the DOM probe showed the selector visible in phase B and hidden in phase C, and the bound vision review reported the targeted symptom resolved, adLayoutResidue absent and remainingInstances empty. It was rejected only on pageIntegrity 'regressed' with damage (empty 'How Do You Feel About This Article?' reaction panels, a footer skeleton) that this selector cannot cause:⁠ in the live page `[id^="in-content-"]` matches exactly two elements, both empty 280px divs inside #⁠articleBody, and the reaction area the review names is not in the page DOM at all. Later attempts reached the 3-run cap for this candidate family, so the rule stays unverified.

## Still visible after the rule

- Below the Disclaimer block at the end of the article, bottom portion of the tile — A visibly large reserved blank band of empty page height after the Disclaimer text, with no article content, no ad creative and no visible label or frame; it matches the empty reserved advertising space described by the reporter.
- Document y=3912..4724 (full tile, article body region below the paragraph beginning "The dollar is the early beneficiary...") — The supplied tile is one uninterrupted blank white band spanning the full 375px width and roughly 812px of page height with no text, image, ad creative, ad label or frame inside it. It sits in the running article flow immediately after the paragraph text that ends mid-sentence at the bottom of the preceding tile, so the reading flow is interrupted by an oversized reserved empty block of the type the reporter described.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

The run instruction's maintainer rules cover exactly this:⁠ a cosmetic rule that hides the annoyance popup when that is enough, which the verified experiment showed it is (page readable, no scroll lock, overlays gone). No rule exists for the domain and no shared multi-domain family matches, so a new domain-scoped cosmetic rule is the correct fix rather than an extend_domains edit. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/ed158e6f05d1dd16659d8d2760888c8b3337c896/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

Cookie Notices filter policy requires declining non-essential cookies by default where possible; the proposed rule clicks the site's own 'reject' link, matching that policy. The reporter's product is AdGuard Mini for Mac (Safari); the syntax guidance states the Safari converter supports scriptlet rules through a separate extension, so this rule kind reaches the reporter's product. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5b27d5277d602abb1a3053fbbb87e23b99251742/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — macworld.com serves an Admiral VRM anti-adblock wall (full-screen "Support Us by Disabling Your Adblocker" modal with html/body scroll lock, loaded from pedaldudes.com) seconds after an article opens. Adding `||pedaldudes.com^$domain=macworld.com` to the Base filter's anti-adblock section removed the wall in the verified A/B/C browser experiment with page integrity intact. ## Rule `||pedaldudes.com^$domain=macworld.com` ## Policy rationale Run instruction:⁠ the site's own advertising, paywalls and German anti-adblock walls are the excluded categories; this is an English-language site running a third-party (Admiral) anti-adblock gate, so none of those exclusions applies. Run instruction:⁠ 'Any other anti-adblock wall:⁠ write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script' - the captured requests (artifact:⁠har:⁠91d34283-47f4-497e-836c-e1bf8b241a43) show the Admiral loader on pedaldudes.com and the page config enable_ad_block:⁠true, so that condition is met. Filter policy:⁠ the wall covers the whole viewport, dims the article and locks html/body scrolling, i.e. it effectively prevents using the website, which the policy lists as grounds to block. Maintainer rules:⁠ a cosmetic hide would not be enough (randomized classes; scroll lock remains), so stopping the loader with a network rule is the correct anti-adblock fix, and no existing shared anti-adblock rule family for this vendor exists to extend. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/fccccbd3d676d0983a26f3557988e77d31b8e6ed/BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On www⁠.ldplayer.net/download/install an empty 1200x300 AdSense slot container (`div#ad-install-top-…`) is left as a blank white band below the header once AdGuard blocks/hides the ad, exactly the region the reporter outlined. Adding `ldplayer.net##div[id^="ad-install-top-"]` to BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt verified in the reporter-profile session:⁠ symptom resolved, page integrity intact, no remaining instances. ## Rule `ldplayer.net##div[id^="ad-install-top-"]` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The run instruction's closing rules (first-party ads, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls, unrelated anti-adblock without a captured detector script) do not apply:⁠ this is an empty leftover container of a third-party Google AdSense unit that filtering already emptied, and there is no anti-adblock wall. Filter policy's protections for the site's own advertising do not apply — the container is an AdSense slot, not first-party advertising. No rule family or existing repository rule already covers this container, so a new site-scoped rule is the correct fix. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/33cfcbf98d4b69f84ffa4af811518c6cc8600058/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 4738](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/33cfcbf98d4b69f84ffa4af811518c6cc8600058/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt#L4738). ## Screenshots

Unfortunately, It is complicated to resolve with a regular adblock rule because the website is being protected by service of Ad-Shield that is an anti-adblock company.

## Userscript Installation
Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

Indeterminate — The report is an in-app ad inside the Yahoo Mail Android app's inbox (sponsored "Rocket Mortgage" row), while its recorded URL is only the app's Play Store listing; that listing loaded fine but has zero ad slots and no ad requests, and the app UI or its webmail counterpart cannot be reached from the locked browser/proxy environment. No evidence-backed rule can be written, so this run ends analysis-only and a maintainer should request the app's AdGuard filtering log to identify the ad request.

- No route or tool for reports whose symptom lives in a native mobile app UI (reported URL is a store listing): Issue #⁠246303 is an AdGuard for Android in-app ad report:⁠ the "Issue URL" field is the Google Play listing for com.yahoo.mobile.client.android.mail, while the reporter screenshot shows a sponsored "Rocket Mortgage … Ad" row inside the Yahoo Mail Android app's inbox. The run instruction's routing only covers "website-filtering reports from AdGuard mobile apps", and the two advertised environments (Chromium extension under test, AdGuard CLI proxy) both drive a browser:⁠ neither can render a native Android app UI nor capture the app's requests. comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"9683ccad6837686a97c52ba85fcbf37c84ffdf0eac1776a57a32eda1990bb116"} -->
The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Not reproduced — The reported "Sponsored" popup on barchart.com did not reproduce:⁠ with the reporter's own imported filter set the fullscreen SPY chart page loaded cleanly and full-page vision found the symptom absent after roughly six minutes of dwelling, with the page's only ad-side loader (asc_prebid.js) already blocked by the Base rule `_prebid.js$script`. No rule is proposed; a maintainer should re-check because the site denied marketing consent in these filtered sessions while an unfiltered control loaded the ad stack and rendered the third-party Braze in-app-message overlay `div.ab-iam-root` that matches the reporter's screenshot.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Run instruction policy rules checked:⁠ this is not the site's own product self-promotion, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall and not any anti-adblock wall (the reporter screenshot shows a 'Sponsored' advertiser popup, not a disable-your-adblock message), and not a scam/phishing page - so no policy rule closes it and rule generation would be allowed. Closure rests on reproduction, not policy:⁠ under the reporter's own imported filter set the reported popup was absent on the successfully loaded reported page (structured full-page vision reporterSymptomPresence 'absent'). Filter-policy criteria retained:⁠ 'The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked' plus the quality requirements (minimal JavaScript rules, no performance or breakage impact) from AdguardTeam/KnowledgeBase filter-policy.md, and the rule-placement section of AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters CONTRIBUTING.md.

## Missing information

- Run instruction gives no handling for a report whose ad symptom is absent because the site's CMP denies marketing consent in the test session: On www⁠.barchart.com the reported "Sponsored" popup never appeared with the reporter's own filter set (prepared AdGuard extension, reporter import). The only ad-side loader the page asked for (hb-barchart.opentrade.ascendeum.com/asc_prebid.js) was blocked by the existing Base rule `_prebid.js$script`, but the site's Cookiebot state in every filtered session recorded `untrusted_consent_marketing: denied` (a CybotCookiebotGpcToast was also on screen), while the unfiltered control recorded marketing granted and rendered the third-party Braze in-app-message overlay `div.ab-iam-root`. The run instruction's `not_reproduced` rule only asks whether the defect is absent on the successfully loaded page; it says nothing about how to weigh a consent-state confound when deciding between propose_close(not_reproduced) and analysis_only, nor whether a consent-gated symptom counts as absent.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41917322818

<sub>Automated analysis against filters at `7175c75`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.</sub>

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The "I use cookies" panel on www⁠.saphysio.co.za is a self-hosted CookieConsent widget (#⁠cc--main) already handled by the shared multi-domain element-hiding rule in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt; the domain-scoped candidate saphysio.co.za#⁠#⁠#⁠cc--main was verified to hide the panel with the page left intact, and the host merges it into that shared rule. ## Rule `saphysio.co.za###cc--main` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie consent notice (annoyance) that the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to block; it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall and not an anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's no-rule rules applies. AdGuard Cookie Notices policy:⁠ hiding the consent notice/script is the standard mechanism when it is sufficient, and here it is — the panel is a bottom bar over already rendered content with no scroll lock and no consent-gated function. Maintainer rule:⁠ when the fix fits an existing shared rule, add the reported domain to that rule rather than write a new one — the #⁠#⁠#⁠cc--main family in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt already handles this consent widget on \~190 sites. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/7175c753df735557cb4aaa29886d6ced8b05c241/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 55](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/7175c753df735557cb4aaa29886d6ced8b05c241/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L55). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41916669985 Automated analysis against filters at `7175c75`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

Verified by A/B/C experiment:⁠ the banner is visible in phase B and hidden in phase C with the page layout intact. ## Rule `dealseek.com##.smart_app_banner` ## Policy rationale The report is a mobile app-install banner, the category the repository's policy defines for the AdGuard Mobile App Banners filter:⁠ 'a filter that blocks banners and popups that encourage visitors to install mobile apps'. It is not the site's own revenue advertising being deliberately unblocked, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's no-rule categories applies. It is not covered by the Mobile App Banners filter's exception for header/menu banners:⁠ the bar is full-width and sticky at the top of the mobile viewport (56 px of an 812 px viewport) and stays there while scrolling, so it distracts through the whole visit. Number of rules is minimal (one domain added to an existing rule), no rule impacts page performance, and no JavaScript rule is used. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/7175c753df735557cb4aaa29886d6ced8b05c241/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — Issue #⁠246308 reports easyway.ua's cookie-consent bar as an annoyance; the reporter's screenshot and the live page both show a first-party fixed bottom "COOKIES / Accept all / Essential only" bar covering content. `easyway.ua##div[role="region"][aria-label="Cookie consent"]` was applied and verified in the AdGuard CLI proxy session:⁠ the bar (227px of an 812px mobile viewport, exactly one match) went from visible to hidden with page integrity intact and no remaining instances, so the rule belongs in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt. ## Rule `easyway.ua##div[role="region"][aria-label="Cookie consent"]` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's filter policy closes only first-party advertising, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls and other anti-adblock reports without a captured detector script; this report is a cookie-consent bar (T:⁠ Annoyance) on a Ukrainian site with no anti-adblock wall at all, so no policy rule blocks a fix. The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists for exactly this symptom per the policy guidance:⁠ 'In most cases, simply hiding or blocking the corresponding scripts is sufficient', and the bar is a first-party Next.js element with no distinct vendor request to block. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/7175c753df735557cb4aaa29886d6ced8b05c241/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Missing information - Reporter settings import cannot be applied on the adguard_cli (proxy) route: Issue #⁠246308 carries an explicit settings import URL (reports.adguard.com/settings/import.html?product_type=and&⁠...). The run instruction says that when the issue provides an import URL the reporter profile is `reported_on_current` with that URL and that only such a session may run apply_rule experiments, and that a defaults_plus_required comparison should follow. In the locked adguard_cli environment, launch_browser requires extension:⁠"none" (per the environment's routing guidance, since the proxy filters and there is no extension to prepare), but launch_browser refuses `settings` for extension:⁠"none" ("A control session (extension \⁠"none\⁠") runs no blocker and takes no \⁠"settings\⁠""), and it only accepts settings with extension:⁠"prepared". The run instruction gives no guidance on how to reconcile the reporter settings profile with a proxy-filtered, extension-less session, so the reporter list set (including EasyList/EasyList Cookie List and the reporter's Stealth Mode options) cannot be reproduced here and the validated baseline is the proxy's own published-filter baseline instead. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41929528006 Automated analysis against filters at `7175c75`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"de8987d04dd78947f448227deee3ecb6c15dde06a5f6669145f5042719e896c9"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported block is an AdGuard DNS resolver "Dangerous website" page from AdGuard DNS's phishing/malware database, not a filter-list rule:⁠ through the locked network-filtering baseline (official AdGuard DNS filter, id 15) sapiensnovus.org loaded HTTP 200 with 0 applied rules and 0 blocked requests, so there is no repository rule to fix and de-listing lies outside this repository.

## Missing information

- No repository guidance for AdGuard DNS security-database (phishing/malware blocklist) false-positive reports: The run instruction's filter policy enumerates first-party ads, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls, other anti-adblock walls and non-anti-adblock scam pages, but says nothing about a report whose complaint is that AdGuard DNS's phishing/malware database blocks the site (issue #⁠246309, labels N:⁠ AdGuard DNS). Nothing states whether such a report may be handled here, belongs to the DNS security team, or should be closed. The locked environment's filterBaseline also recorded the reporter's actual filtering source, 'AdGuard DNS security filter (phishing and malware protection)', only as skippedSources with kind unresolved_name, so the run has no baseline for the filtering the reporter uses and cannot reproduce or validate a fix for it. In addition, the linked filter-syntax/policy/contributing documents cover filter rules only and say nothing about de-listing domains from the DNS security database.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41935219174
